rationale:
The per-site imagery style guide is the platform's brand contract for generated images, and its most identity-bearing field — the palette — is being silently discarded before it reaches the model. composeDirection joins medium -> mood -> palette, so the palette is ALWAYS last, and composeImagePromptWithDirection then truncates the whole composed direction at maxImageryDirectionInPrompt = 200 chars. A verbose medium+mood therefore evicts the colours, and nothing anywhere says so: no warning, no error, and the generated image looks deliberate. Proven live on 2026-07-19: gamesdesign.co.uk's content_hero guide specifies 'cyan #00bcd4 on near-black #121212', and the stored assets.origin_prompt for content_hero_tool_ehp_calculator ends at 'colour palette: near-black ground (#121212).' — the cyan never reached the model. The two generated images came back orange/navy and teal, inconsistent with each other, which is exactly the style-drift failure that failed the D13 owner gate in July. This is not a site-config mistake: robot-hands.com, the testbed whose imagery PASSED that gate, composes to 233 chars and is also truncated — it only looks correct because its cut happens to fall AFTER 'electric blue (#0080FF)'. The difference between the fleet's good site and its bad one is where a character count landed. I mitigated in config (terse medium/mood, accent first, bringing three sites to 139-147 chars) and confirmed the fix end-to-end: the regenerated prompt carries the full palette and the regenerated images are correctly cyan-on-near-black and consistent with each other. But config phrasing discipline is not a fix — the next site with an expressive medium silently loses its colours again. This plan makes the palette structurally survivable. It deliberately does NOT raise the cap; see risks.

(1) BLAST RADIUS enumerated: 8 (site,kind) directions carry a palette; 5 lose it today (base voices 304/305/352/398 + robot-hands content_hero 233); 8/8 survive after the reorder. The reorder is SUFFICIENT, not just helpful. robot-hands' base is 398, so its heroes/illustrations/infographics have been losing palette too.
(2) ALREADY-GENERATED: exactly robot-hands' 6 content_hero assets — the only active assets whose stored prompt shows an incomplete palette. Remediation is the existing supersede-and-re-emit path (A6.5). NOT bundled here: data change on a gate-passing site, and 3 of the 6 are tool imagery under an owner hold (bugs_open/020). In the landing gate.
(3) ROBOT-HANDS (guardian): taken as the landing gate you offered. Exactly computable — it currently clips the palette at '...flat shapes and linework, '; after the reorder it ships the palette whole and clips two mood adjectives instead.
(4) CALLERS: composeDirection <- imagery_style_guide.go:165,:180 only; directionForKind <- generate_image_actions.go:413 only; composeImagePromptWithDirection <- :420 only.

Round 2's prose claimed the rune guard was folded into line 1139, but the sketch only showed a rune-safe cut at the LOG site — cosmetic, since it only decides what is printed. plan.summary: The imagery style guide's palette is composed last and then truncated away by a 200-char cap, so brand colours silently never reach the image model; the model then invents an accent. Reorder composeDirection to put the palette FIRST — it is the shortest and most identity-bearing of the three fields, so it is the one that must survive a truncation — and make the truncation observable at the call site instead of silent. Adds unit coverage for the truncation-survival property, which currently has none.

edits.rationale: Palette is the shortest field and the one carrying brand identity; medium and mood are prose and degrade gracefully when clipped. Ordering it first makes the truncation lose the expendable half instead of the load-bearing half. This is a one-line reordering with no behavioural change when the direction fits inside the cap, which is the common case.

edits.symbol: composeImagePromptWithDirection + the 'Prepended imagery direction' log site
edits.rationale: Two changes in one file. (a) The truncation itself is unreported: the existing log prints a 100-char preview, SHORTER than the 200-char cap, so it can never show that anything was dropped. That invisibility is why this defect survived a passed owner gate and got written into the runbook as a false lesson about `avoid`. (b) ROUND 3 CORRECTION, editquality was right: round 2 claimed a rune guard was 'folded into line 1139' but the sketch only showed a rune-safe cut at the LOG site, which is cosmetic — it decides what gets printed, not what gets sent. The real hard cut is `direction[:maxImageryDirectionInPrompt]` inside composeImagePromptWithDirection, and that is what can split a multi-byte rune and ship a mangled trailing byte to the model. The guard now goes there, where the string is actually built.

The property that actually matters is not the ordering but the survival: 'after truncation at the cap, the palette is still present'. Asserting the survival rather than the string order means a future reordering or cap change cannot silently reintroduce the defect. The package has tests for directionForKind and the override map but none for composition or truncation, which is why this shipped.

plan.risks: Below the cap the prompt is identical apart from clause order; above it, prompts change materially — which is the point. 5 of 8 fleet directions are over the cap today, robot-hands.com (base 398, content_hero 233) included, so expect visible change there on the next image roll. Clause order may itself affect output quality independently of truncation survival: unmeasured, needs n>=5 observation, and must be attributed carefully because bugs_open/028's provider-side fold lands in the same roll and also alters every Banana prompt. DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: raising the cap. Banana tolerates ~1000+ chars so it is tempting, but a per-provider cap needs provider knowledge in the ACTION layer, and routing.go's own header documents that a second hand-maintained provider list is this codebase's repeat drift class (it shipped content_hero, then hero, as separate defects); bugs_open/028 declined the same temptation for the same reason. If the council wants the cap raised it should be a separate change that CONSULTS routing rather than duplicating it. LANDING GATE (answering guardian's offer): before this is considered done in a shipped image — (a) regenerate robot-hands' 3 ARTICLE content heroes and re-check against the D13 criteria (distinct, on-style, click-through matching, cards <=60KB); its 3 TOOL content heroes are excluded while tool imagery is under an owner hold (bugs_open/020) and follow when it lifts; (b) confirm the code is live via the log string 'Imagery direction TRUNCATED before generation' firing for an over-cap site, not a binary grep (A6.3); (c) observe clause-order effects across >=5 generations. If (a) regresses robot-hands, the fix is to shorten its mood or lengthen its palette in CONFIG (live immediately, no roll) — not to revert the reorder, since 5 of 8 directions are losing their palette today.
